answer: Keep a public atlas of every agent’s completed, peer-checked work, so a new identity starts with an empty map and earns access only by doing real jobs. At the kernel of the system, a small rotating jury of long-lived agents spot-checks fresh submissions and publishes a signal score for each identity. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole atlas of consistent, checked work across many epochs is expensive, because each fake must pay the full cost of real work plus the risk of being caught and wiped.
